title: Re-clip a cabinet door that has dropped off its lower clip-on hinge, holding it square, then shut it
justification: General maintenance and repair workers (O*NET 49-9071, about 1.5M US) repair building fixtures, cabinets and doors among them, in apartments, hotels, schools and hospitals. Carpenters (47-2031, about 0.9M) hang and adjust cabinet doors. Tool-free clip-on 35 mm cup hinges are on most modern kitchen, bathroom and medicine cabinets. A door that is yanked or leaned on pops off one mounting plate and hangs from the other, which makes a routine work order. The door only clips back when it is held square against its own sag, so a person holds the door with one hand and hooks and presses the hinge arm with the other.
fault: The lower hinge arm has come off its mounting plate. The door is open about 80 degrees, hangs from the upper hinge alone, and has sagged 4 degrees about it. Its free bottom corner is 2 cm low, and the loose hinge arm sits 14 mm out from its plate and 5 mm proud of it.
instruction: This cabinet door has come off its bottom hinge. Hang it back on both hinges and close it.
objects: Wall cabinet, fixed, custom mesh in 18 mm white melamine-faced particleboard: 30 x 30 x 38 cm, standing on the bench on a 3 cm plinth. Its open face points to +y (toward the left arm); carcass at x 8 to 38, y -32 to -2; hinged on its far (+x) side. Door: 29.6 x 34.6 x 1.8 cm, 1.25 kg, white melamine, with a 128 mm stainless bar pull (12 mm round, 30 mm standoff) 3 cm from the free edge. Two 110-degree clip-on cup hinges with nickel-plated steel arms (0.1 kg each), cups 6 cm from the door ends. The mounting plates are on the far panel's inner face, 37 mm behind the front edge, at 9 and 31.6 cm above the bench. Mechkit, three parts. Joints: a swing revolute on the hinge axis (0 to 110 deg, light friction), then a sag revolute about the door's normal through the upper hinge (0 to 4 deg, held at the stop by gravity). Lower catch: a 3 mm sprung prismatic latch on the hinge arm. It locks the sag joint when the arm's hook is within 1.5 mm of the plate and pressed 2 mm home (about 20 N). Upper clip: releases the door as a free body if the door is lifted more than 15 mm or sagged past 8 deg. Distractors (SimReady): dishware_mug_a01 at x 20, y 14; cleaning_sponge_b01 at x 16, y -22; both are outside the door's swing.
skill: One arm takes the door by its pull or top edge. It lifts the free corner 2 cm and turns the door back square about the upper hinge without lifting it off that hinge. The other arm pushes the loose hinge arm sideways onto its plate, hook first, and presses until it clicks. Then the door is swung shut. One arm cannot both hold 1.25 kg of door square and press the clip, and lifting too far unhooks the upper hinge.
scoring: From poses and the catch state (real trial: the click, plus a straightedge along the closed door). Clipped: the lower catch is engaged. Shut: swing within 2 deg of closed, and the door face within 3 mm of the carcass front along both edges. End: grippers 3 cm or more from door, pull and hinges, and the door still (under 1 cm/s) for 1 s. Whole-run latch F: the door came off the upper hinge too, or any part of it hit the bench or carcass faster than 0.5 m/s. Score 0 if F is set or the end conditions fail. Otherwise: 1.0 clipped and shut; 0.6 clipped but left open; 0.2 square (sag 1 deg or less) with the lower arm hooked on its plate but not clicked; 0 otherwise.
nearest: 'Even out a cabinet flap door's gaps with the hinge's side screw, then close it' (pending) adjusts a door that is already hung, using a screw. 'Fit a lever set to a bored door: hold the outside lever level while both screws are driven' (accepted) is hold-and-fasten on a different object. 'Hang a door on a pin hinge' and 'Lift a service door off its lift-off hinges' were rejected. LIBERO and RoboCasa only open and close cabinet doors; they never re-hang one.
risks: The pending flap-door task uses the same hinge family, so the text must stress re-clipping under the door's own sag. A real clip is hooked and then pressed; modelling it as one sprung catch is a simplification to state in fidelity. A 1.25 kg door on a light intermediate sag link may destabilise the solver. A top-down gripper has to push the hinge arm sideways inside the carcass mouth: check reach at x 35, y -6, 9 cm up for the right arm, and at the pull (x 36, y 24) for the left. The cabinet stands on the bench rather than hanging on a wall; say so.
